raw_response:
Cotton, like always. Twelve mu, same as every year. Let me think through how I'll do it this season.

---

My land here on the west side of the village, it's got those salty patches in places — wheat doesn't do so well on it, so my old man grew cotton and I've been growing cotton on this same dirt for thirty years. I know every corner of it. The folks closer to the river do the wheat-maize, but for us cotton is what works.

Just me and the wife in the house now. The boy is in the city, sends money when he can but he's not coming back to pull cotton bolls. So every decision I make, I'm thinking about what two pairs of hands can do. The picking in autumn, that's the hard part — last year my back was crying by the end of it. I'll probably get my niece and her husband to come down for a few days at the peak, give them some money or some cotton to take home.

**Seed.** I buy the hybrid bag from the supply shop in town, same one everyone in our village buys. The seller knows what does well around here. It's the kind that the bollworms leave alone — Bt they call it. Before that seed came around, the bollworm used to eat us up. Costs about 70 yuan a mu but I won't go back to the cheap seed.

**Mulch film.** I lay the plastic film like everybody does. Without it the seedlings come up weak and the weeds choke them. One roll does about a mu and a half. Maybe 30 yuan a mu when I figure it.

**Fertilizer.** I do it the way I always do. When I'm making the ridges before planting, I put down one bag of the compound — the 15-15-15 kind — per mu. Then around June when the cotton is squaring, I put down maybe half a bag of urea per mu to push it along. Two times, that's it. One year my cousin told me the extension fellow said to put more, so I tried it on two mu — didn't see much difference, just spent more money. Went back to my way.

**Water.** I share a well with three other families. The pump runs on electricity and you have to pay for it now, it's not free like the old days. I water once if the seedlings look thirsty after planting, and once more when the bolls are filling out. Two times usually. Last year was dry so I had to do three and the bill hurt. If the rain comes good in July maybe just one.

**Spraying.** Cotton is no easy crop, the bugs come at you all summer. Aphids first, then the plant bugs (盲蝽), then sometimes the little spider mites if it gets hot and dry. I spray maybe five or six times across the season — whatever the supply shop sells, mix it the way the bottle says, sometimes a little stronger if the bugs are bad. Also a herbicide before I plant to keep the weeds down.

**Tillage.** I plow after the cold breaks in March. My neighbor has the small tractor, I pay him to come in for a half day to turn the soil and make the ridges. Faster than the old way with the ox.

**Yield.** Last year I picked about 270 jin of seed cotton per mu. Year before was a bit less because of the rain at the wrong time. If the weather is normal I'm hoping for the same again. Don't dream too big, just hope for the same.
